Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /reˈku.pe.ro/
  • Rhymes: -upero
  • Hyphenation: re‧cù‧pe‧ro

Etymology 1

[edit]

Deverbal from recuperare +‎ -o.

Noun

[edit]

recupero m (plural recuperi)

  1. recovery
  2. salvage, rescue
  3. recycling, reclamation, reclaim
  4. making up, remedial
  5. rehabilitation (criminals etc.)
  6. (sports) replay
    minuti di recupero ― extra time
  7. retrieval
Related terms
[edit]
  • recuperare

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

recupero

  1. first-person singular present indicative of recuperare

Latin

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [rɛˈkʊ.pɛ.roː]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [reˈkuː.pe.ro]

Verb

[edit]

recuperō (present infinitive recuperāre, perfect active recuperāvī, supine recuperātum); first conjugation

  1. alternative form of reciperō (“regain, restore, restore to health”)

Descendants

[edit]
  • Italo-Romance:
    • Italian: ricoverare, ricovrare
    • Neapolitan: recupetà
    • ⇒ Sicilian: rinchìpitu
    • Old Venetan: recovrare
      • Venetan: regroarse (reflexive)
  • Gallo-Italic:
    • Emilian: archervar
    • Old Lombard: recrovare, recrovar
  • Gallo-Romance:
    • Northern:
      • Old Franco-Provençal: recouvrar, recorar
        • Franco-Provençal: rcoverá, recoubrà, recoublar
      • Old French: recovrer
    • Southern:
      • Catalan: recobrar
      • Occitan: recobrar, recrobar
  • Ibero-Romance:
    • Old Galician-Portuguese: recobrar
      • Galician: recobrar
      • Portuguese: recobrar
    • Old Spanish: recobrar, recombrar
      • Spanish: recobrar
  • ⇒ Vulgar Latin:
    • *cuperāre (see there for further descendants)
  • Borrowings:
    • → English: recuperate
    • → French: récupérer
      • → Romanian: recupera
    • → Galician: recuperar
    • → Italian: recuperare, ricuperare
    • → Portuguese: recuperar
    • → Spanish: recuperar

[edit]
  • Walther von Wartburg (1928–2002), “rĕcŭpĕrare”, in Französisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch, volume 10: R, page 165

Further reading

[edit]
  • “recupero”, in Charlton T. Lewis (1891), An Elementary Latin Dictionary, New York: Harper & Brothers
  • “recupero”, in Gaffiot, Félix (1934), Dictionnaire illustré latin-français, Hachette.
  • Carl Meißner; Henry William Auden (1894), Latin Phrase-Book‎[1], London: Macmillan and Co.
    • to recover liberty: libertatem recuperare
